title: The best kits we didn’t see at the 2026 World Cup
text:
FIFA World

Cup 2026

Curaçao's away shirt (left) was one many fans hoped to see at the World Cup, but the team never wore it. Chile's (right) fell victim to the team's failure to qualify. Photos courtesy of Adidas

The Athletic has live coverage of France vs Morocco in the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

So much has happened in the 2026 World Cup that you’d be forgiven for not realizing several teams went home before wearing every kit they brought to the tournament.

How does this happen? FIFA oversees which kits are worn in matches to avoid overlapping colors that make opposing teams look too similar, with priority given to the designated “home” team. That can result in a team wearing the same kit several matches in a row and then being eliminated before they get a chance to switch it up.

Advertisement

In some cases, this is nothing to lose sleep over, but in others it’s nothing short of a sartorial travesty. To make up for the injustice of some of the tournament’s best kits never being seen on a World Cup pitch, here are five that didn’t get the spotlight they deserved before their team’s elimination.

1. Curaçao away

We warned this was likely to happen before the tournament began and, sadly, it came true. Curaçao did not wear its lovely away kit in any of its three group matches at the World Cup, yet the kit still sold out before the opening ceremony. The Athletic’s Nick Miller ranked it as the No. 1 away kit of the tournament, featuring a pastel yellow background and vibrant stripes inspired by the colors of the buildings in capital city Willemstad. Curaçao did wear the kit in a pre-tournament friendly against Scotland, so it wasn’t completely wasted, but that’s not the same, is it?

2. South Africa away

This is another wonderful effort from Adidas that went unused because South Africa never changed out of its yellow home shirt for its four World Cup matches. This one has a bit of a ’90s vibe with the collar and subtle design work within the vertical stripes on the dark green shirt. An excellent top that deserved a run out.

3. Ivory Coast away

Like Curaçao’s away kit, Puma’s Ivory Coast away shirt also sold out despite not being worn at the tournament. The soft-washed green-and-orange print gives it a perfect look for a summer World Cup while still identifiably representing The Elephants.

4. DR Congo away

DR Congo brought three kits to the World Cup and used its red-and-yellow third look before its away kit, leaving Umbro’s white-and-light blue design as the odd one out in the team’s four matches. The geometric pattern at the bottom of the shirt (which also runs down the sides of the shorts) fading into solid white at the top is a unique twist on the standard white kit befitting the game’s top stage. Alas, it didn’t quite make it.

Advertisement

5. Haiti original designs

Unlike the others on this list, we didn’t see Haiti’s original World Cup kit designs because of color clashes or the team’s early exit — but because of a late decision from FIFA. Shortly before the tournament began, FIFA decided the scene on the bottom of the shirts — a group of men raising a red-and-blue flag at the Battle of Vertiéres shortly before Haitian independence was declared — was too political and had to be removed. Haiti’s kitmaker, Saeta, produced new versions of the team’s kits without the imagery, and the result wasn’t the same.

The original versions of Haiti’s home and away shirts can still be purchased, however.

And what about teams that didn’t qualify for the tournament? Some gems in that category deserve to be seen, too.

1. Costa Rica away

Los Ticos missed out on the World Cup for the first time since 2010, and what cruel timing given the away kit lined up for this one. The bold, tropical vibe would have been a welcome addition to the designs on display at this World Cup.

2. Chile away

Representing the wildflowers of the Atacama Desert, Chile’s away kit is another distinctive look that would have been great to see at the tournament. This effort was particularly futile, however, since Chile finished bottom of the CONMEBOL qualifying table and has missed three consecutive World Cups.

3. Jamaica away

Jamaica narrowly missed out on qualifying for the World Cup, losing to DR Congo in extra time of its playoff final, and denying the tournament the Bob Marley-inspired Reggae Boyz tribute kits. The away design features soundwave patterns and vinyl record graphics in honor of the Jamaican music legend. You can almost hear “Buffalo Soldier” when looking at it.

4. Northern Ireland away

This shirt is almost too nice, even for the World Cup. You could wear it to a wedding, and you wouldn’t look out of place.

Advertisement

5. Italy away

This one may look like a plain white shirt from a distance, but if you look closely you’ll see a lovely, subtle pattern throughout.

And yes, Adidas made all five jerseys in the best-among-non-qualifiers category. When the 2026 World Cup participants were finalized, Adidas’ designers must have been in tears.
